2. In this suit plaintiffs 1-30 as heirs of original owner Faloo's two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi claimed l/3rd share in the suit property. According to the plaintiffs C.S. plot No. 545 measuring .63 acre, C.S. plot No. 232 measuring .38 acre, C.S. plot No. 676 measuring .22 acre C.S. plot No. 953 measuring .15 acre, and C.S. plot No. 640 measuring .34 acre (total area = 1.72 acre) of C.S. Khatian No. 48, Touzi No. 192 of mouza Jatrabari, P.S. Kseraniganj, District Dhaka originally belonged to Faloo (see Ext.1). Similarly C.S. plot No. 533 measuring .34 acre. C.S. plot No. 678 measuring .21 acre., C.S. plot No. 667 measuring .15 acre; C.S. plot No. 630 measuring .47 acre, C.S. plot No. 954 measuring .16 acre, C.S. plot No. 973 measuring .30 acre and C.S. plot No. 989 measuring .17 (total area = 1.80) of Khatian No. 53, Touzi No. 112 of Mouza Jatrabari, P.S. Keraniganj, District Dhaka belonged to Faloo alias Sk. Faloo as Jote Faloo (রায়তিস্বত্বে স্থিতিবান)= occupancy raiyat. Fa- 100 had 16 annas raiyaty right in the aforessid plots of the said two Khatians, While he was owning and possessing the aforesaid lands in assertion of his right and title, he died before the last settlement operation leaving behind his two sons, namely Khadem and Chamoo and his two daughters namely, Joy tonnessa and Anwara Bibi as heirs to his aforessid jote. Each of his sons (Khadem and Chamoo) got 1/3rd share and each of his two daughter (Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi) 1/6th share in the said properties (described in the schedule of the plaint including amendment made in the plaint) left by Faloo. The aforesaid two sons and two daughters of Faloo had been in joint ownership and possession of the properties in their respective snare. Khadem, as the eldest son of Faloo, taking advantage of the confidence of his two sisters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi got his name surreptitiously recorded in the last settlement record as 16 annas owner of the aforesaid C.S. Khatian No. 48 containing C.S. plot Nos. 545, 632, 679,953 and 740. Similarly Sk. Chamoo, the second son of late Faloo, got his own name recorded as 16 ann as owner' of C.S. Khatian No. 53 containing the aforesaid C.S. plot Nos. 533, 678, 667, 630, 954, 973 and 989 in the last settlement record. It is apparent that the last settlement records showing Khadem as exclusive owner in possession of the aforesaid plots of Khatian No. 48 and showing Chamoo as exclusive owner in possession of the aforesaid plots of Khatian No. 53 is wrong. While Khadem, Chamoo, Joytonnessa and Anwara were in joint possession and ownership of the suit properties in their respective shares, Chamoo died leaving three sons, namely, late Magon, Danajuddin (defendant No. 3) and Moghal Mia (defendant No. 2) and two daughters, namely Safura Bibi (defendant No. 8) and Late Hazera Bibi. Thus the entire share of Chamoo devolved upon his aforesaid sons and daughters. Thereafter Hazera Bibi died leaving her sole heir Azimuddin (defendant No. 9). Thereafter Magon died leaving one son, namely, Shahabuddin (defendant No. 4), two daughters, namely Latifan and Ashrafan (defendant Nos. 5 and 6 respectively) and window Ayesha Khatun (defendant No. 7). After the death of Chamoo, his sister Joytonnessa died leaving one son Korban, three daughters, namely Akmolnessa, Orfan and Sayera Khatun. One sixth (1/6th) share of Joytunnessa thus devolved upon her said son Korban and the said three daughters-Akmolnessa, Orfannessa and Sayera. Thereafter Akmolnessa died leaving her son Afajuddin (defendant No.8) as her only heir to her estate. Thereafter Orfannessa alias Orfa died leaving two sons, namely Serajuddin (plaintiff No. 97 and Jahed Ali and one daughter Seha Bibi (plaintiff No. 11) as her heirs in the suit properties. Then Jahed Ali, son of late Orfannessa, died leaving his son Tahed Ali (plaintiff No. 10) as his sole heir to his estate. Late Joytonnessa's daughter Sayera Khatun thereafter died leaving her two sons, Safajuddin (plaintiff No. 12) and Osimuddin (plaintiff No. 13) and one daughter Asadan Bibi (plaintiff No. 14) as heirs to her estate. Late Joytonnessa's son Korban Ali died leaving behind six sons, namely Abdul Aziz, Aminuddin, Amiruddin, Abdul Hye, Wajuddin and Hafizuddin (plaintiffs 1-6 respectively) and a widow Aimon Nessa (plaintiff No. 7) as his heirs. 

 6. The further case for the plaintiff is that while the plaintiffs were in joint ownership and possession of the suit properties aforesaid C.S. plots No. 545, 632 and 679 of Khatian No. 48 and C.S Nos. 533, 678, 630 and 989 of Khatian No. 53 were acquired by the Collector of Dhaka in L.A. Case No. 92 of 1963-64 for WAPDA Project. The plaintiffs learnt on 27.11.64 that the defendants have surreptitiously got the award prepared in their names and arc trying to get all the compensation money for the acquired plots of land fraudulently suppressing the fact that the plaintiffs are also co-sharers to the extent of 1/3rd share of the compensation money. 

 8. Defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo (daughter of late Khadem) and defendant No.10 Khoaj Bibi, another daughter of late Khadem, contested the suit by filing two separate written statements. Defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo contended that she is the daughter of Khadem through Khadem's second wife Korfulnessa and that defendant No.10 Khoaj Bibi alias Makhari is the daughter of Khadem through Khadem's 1st wife Soal Bibi. During the life time of Khadcm he, on 28.2.1917 corresponding to 16th Falgoon, 1322 B.S., gifted by heba-bil-ewaj to Korfulnessa dag No. 953 (homestead with hut), dag No.545 and dag No. 632 of khatian No. 48 of Mouza Jatrabari. Korfulnessa in her turn made a gift on 7.6.1939 A.D. corresponding to 24th Jaistra1346 B.S. of plot No. 953 (having tin hut), plot No. 545 and plot No. 632 of Mouza Jatrabari (Khatian No. 48) to her daughter defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo and her son-in-law and Lal Banoo's husband, added defendant No. 20, Amjad Ali by registered deed of gift. Defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo and her husband defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali are in exclusive possession in the said three plots by virtue of gift and by adverse possession and the plaintiffs have no subsisting shares or interest in the said three plots. Though defendant No. 1 claimed to have paid rent in her name and in her husband's name but no rent receipt could be produced by defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 20 at the time of trial. 

 9. Defendant No. 10 Khoaj Bibi alias Mukhari contested the suit by filing a written statement to the effect that late Khadem's first wife Soal Bibi died leaving her daughter defendant No. 10 Khoaj Bibi alias Mukhari as her heir. Khadem transferred during his life time C.S. plot No. 740 of Khatian No. 48 to Kazimuddin on 9.12.18 and also gave C.S. plot No. 679 of Khatian No.48 to his daughter Soal Bibi after whose death her daughter Khoaj Bibi alias Mukhari possessed plot No. 679 exclusively for more than 30 years adversely by paying rent. Transferee Kazimuddin died leaving behind his son defendant No. 21 Mullak Chand as his sole heir. During the pendency of the suit defendant No. 21 Mullak Chand died leaving behind his heir defendant No. 21(a) Pari Banoo, wife of Bojumkar Ali. 

 10. The plaintiffs and defendants 2-9 who are the heirs and successors of late Faloo's son late Chamoo filed a petition of compromise on 26.1.65 agreeing to the genealogy as given by the plaintiffs and also admitting the entitlement of 1/3rd share of the plaintiffs in both the suit Khatian Nos. 48 and 53 as heirs successors of late Faloo's two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi. 

 12. Plaintiffs examined two witnesses P.W. 1 Abdul Aziz (plaintiff No. 1) and P.W. 2 Dadan Miah. On behalf of the contesting defendants six witnesses were examined, namely, D.W. 1 Lal Banoo (defendant No. 1), D.W. 2 Mohabbat Ali Sarder, D.W. 3 Amjad Ali (defendant No. 20), D.W. No. 4 Khoaj Bibi alias Makhari (defendant No. 10), D.W. No. 5 Shamsuddin and D.W. No. 6 Reajuddin. Both the parties filed certain Exts. Ext. 1 is the certified copy of C.S. Khatian No. 48 of Mouza Jatrabari. Ext. D is the certified copy of C.S. khatian No. 53 of Mouza Jatrabari. Ext. A is the certified copy of the registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj executed by late Faloo's son late Khadem on 28.2.1917 in favour of his wife Korfulnessa, but for obvious reason it contained no plot number. Ext. A(1) is another deed of gift executed by Korfulnessa to her daughter defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo executed on 7.6.1939 in favour of Korfulnessa and her husband defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali transferring plot Nos. 953, 545 and 632 measuring 1.31 acre. Ext.B-B(5) are provisional rent receipts showing payment of rents for the Bengali Year 1362, 1363,1364, 1365, 1366 and 1368 showing payment of rent by Amjad Ali (defendant No. 20) and Lal Banoo defendant No. 1 in respect of 1.16 acre of land of khatian No.48 of mouza Jatrabari. Ext. No. C is the certified copy of the registered deed showing transfer of 34 acre of plot No. 740 of khatian No. 48 of mouza Jatrabari by Sk. Khadem on 9.12.1918 A.D. in favour of late Kazimuddin, father of defendant No.21 Mullak Chand. 

 13. The learned Subordinate Judge found that the suit is maintainable in its present form as undisputedly all necessary persons having interest in the suit properties have been added as parties to the suit and also because all the joint properties have been brought into the hatchpotch since the plaintiffs made necessary amendments in the plaint and in the schedule to the plaint to meet the objection raised by the contesting defendants in their written statement that the suit properties originally belonged to Faloo from whom his two sons Khadem and Chamoo and his two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi inherited the suit properties, that although the name of Khadem is recorded in khatian No. 48 and the name of Chamoo is recorded in khatian No. 53, but it is also recorded in the khatian that the joie in the said two khatians belonged to Faloo and that therefore the share of two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara by inheritance 1/3rd share remained unaffected; that the defendant failed to prove that Faloo made any gift of the suit properties in favour of his two sons Khalem and Chamoo to the exclusion of his two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi, that even if it is believed that Khadem made a gift of some land of the suit properties and that Khadem's wife Korfulnessa in her turn made a gift of the same to her daughter Lal Banoo and her son-in-law defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali, the fact remains that Khadem is not entitled to make any gift to his daughter beyond the share to which he is entitled to in the suit properties and consequently Khadem's daughter Korfulnessa could not have made any gift to defendant No.1 Lal Banoo and Lal Banoo's husband defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali beyond the 1/3rd share of Khadem in the suit property, that the plaintiffs being co-sharers by inheritance must be and still are in constructive possession of the suit property when there is no total ouster either by stranger or by other co-sharers including contesting defendant and defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali in assertion of their exclusive title, that as the contesting defendants have failed to prove that there is total ouster of the plaintiffs from the suit properties by possession of the defendants by openly denying the title of any sort of the plaintiffs within their (plaintiffs) knowledge; that therefore the fact that the co-sharer out of physical possession remains in constructive possession of the suit land through the other co-sharers remains unrebutted, that the suit by the plaintiffs is therefore not barred by adverse possession by the defendants and the plaintiffs are entitled to 1/3rd share of the suit property as heirs of Faloo's two daughters Joytonnessa and Anwara Bibi. 

 15. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the two appellants submits that the suit land is in possession of the defendant appellants for more than 50 years, that the defendant-appellants are in possession of plot No. 943 measuring.15 acre of Khatian No. 48 of Mouza Jatrabari on the basis of their deed of gift, that they are also in possession of plot No. 545 measuring .36 acre and plot No. 632 measuring .38 acre of said Khatian No. 48 which have been acquired by the government and that the trial Court erroneously held that Faloo did not transfer the suit land in favour of his two sons. Thus he argued that the two defendant-appellants possessed the said three plots adversely to the exclusion of the plaintiff for more than 12 years and thereby acquired title in the said land by adverse possession. 

 16. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondents supported the judgment of the learned subordinate Judge. He how-ever pointed out that it is apparent on the face of the record that the correction of plot No. 953 of khatian No. 48 by substituting plot No. 935 is not correct and is a clerical error in view of the khatian Ext. 1 and that the said plot should continue to be read ac plot No. 953 of khatian No. 48 in the schedule to the plaints as it was originally so. 

 19. D.W.1 Lal Banoo (defendant No. 1) stated that her mother Korfulnessa got land by gift from her father Khadem and that her mother Korfulnessa made a gift of that land to her. She stated that she paid rents and the receipts have been filed by her in Court.We find that the six rent receipts Ext. B-B(5) are provisional rent receipts showing payment of rent for 1.16 acre of land of khatian No.48 of Mouza Jatrabari by defendant No. 1 Lal Banoo and her husband defendant No. 20 Amjad Ali for the period from 1362 B.S. to 1372 B.S. It is significant to note that the contesting defendant appellants failed to produce any rent receipt whatsoever for any period before 1362 B.S. From the six provisional rent receipts Ext. B-Ext. B(5) no presumption of possession can be made. 

 Thus it is clear that right, title and interest of the plaintiffs to the extent of 1/3rd share of the suit property as heirs of Faloo's aforesaid two daughters has not been extinguished by any ouster or adverse possession by the appellants. The Yearned subordinate Judge, therefore, has rightly declared the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs to the extent of 1/ 3rd share of the suit including C.S. plot No.953 of Khatian No.48 of mouza Jatrabari.
